executive_summary:
Your RED status is driven entirely by geopolitical concentration risk, not financial distress or supplier insolvency. Five of your nine at-risk suppliers sit in China (Huizhou BYD, Smoore, IP Sun, Porton, EVE Energy), all flagged for the same US-China trade war and Taiwan exposure; these cover your most critical categories (EMS and batteries) and represent your largest exposure surface. The remaining geopolitical risks cluster into secondary theaters: Stora Enso and ITC near NATO/Russia and India-Pakistan borders respectively, while Sappi's South African energy crisis is operationally concerning but lower priority. GPI's stock movement is isolated noise without a confirmed trigger—monitor but don't act yet.

Urgent action: initiate dual-sourcing conversations immediately for EMS and battery suppliers outside China, and stress-test your Taiwan-linked supply tiers (where chip controls could cascade). The printing substrate and filter material risks (Stora Enso, Tae Young, Sappi) are medium-term; they're real but give you weeks to develop contingency plans before they bite. Your macro environment is stable (EU data confirmed), so this is a supplier geography problem, not a demand cliff.
